functions.funcDef: Produce and control propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans produce thrust for all flight phases; in: fuel at pump inlet, throttle/reverse commands from flight deck; out: thrust, engine parameter data to AVI (SDD §5.1.2, §5.1.4). Independence: left and right engine pairs in separate zones, services not commingled outboard of wing root (SDD §5.1.5).

functions.funcDef: Produce and control propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Two inboard-engine thrust reversers provide ground deceleration; in: reverse command, weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement; out: reverse thrust (SDD §5.1.2). Independence: reverser deployment inhibited in flight by WoW and RA agreement with mechanical sleeve lock (SDD §5.1.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers command roll; ailerons on HYD B and C; in: inceptor/autopilot command, air/inertial data; out: surface position to AVI (SDD §5.3.2, §5.3.4). Independence: dual actuation from different hydraulic systems per surface (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: All-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser with elevators command pitch; elevators on HYD A and C; in: inceptor/autopilot command, air/inertial data; out: surface position to AVI (SDD §5.3.2). Independence: mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim survives loss of all three FCCs (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Split rudder in upper and lower segments commands yaw; upper on HYD A, lower on HYD B; in: inceptor/autopilot command; out: surface position (SDD §5.3.2). Independence: each segment has own actuation and own hydraulic supply; sizing case is outboard engine failure at V1 with max blade payload (SDD §5.3.2, §5.3.3).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps (four sections) and full-span leading-edge slats set high-lift configuration; two PDUs via common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes; in: flap/slat command; out: high-lift position to performance computation (SDD §5.3.2, §5.3.4). Independence: two independent PDUs but a common torque shaft (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Three dissimilar flight control computers vote on command and provide envelope protection in the normal control law; in: air/inertial data, inceptor position; out: envelope protection status, degraded-law annunciation (SDD §5.3.2, §5.3.6). Independence: three computers each on a different electrical source in three separate bays (SDD §5.3.2, §5.3.5).

functions.funcDef: Deliver fuel to the engines and manage distribution of fuel mass across the airframe (SDD §5.2.1). Note: fuel storage/supply is a Resource (§2.1); this captures the distribution/CG-management behaviour the aircraft performs.
functions.subDef: Schedule tank transfer and cross-feed to hold CG and wing bending within limits; imbalance annunciated at 1,200 kg, limited to 3,000 kg; in: fuel management panel/avionics commands; out: CG contribution to loading computation (SDD §5.2.2, §5.2.3, §5.2.6). Independence: single spanwise cross-feed gallery is the only path between sides (SDD §5.2.2).

functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces and absorb landing and taxi loads (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: One nose unit and six main bogies (20 tyres) support the aircraft and absorb landing/taxi loads with flotation for semi-prepared surfaces; retraction/extension on HYD A with free-fall alternate; in: gear lever, WoW; out: gear position (SDD §5.6.2, §5.6.3). Independence: free-fall extension independent of hydraulic pressure; dual independent downlock sensing (SDD §5.6.3). Gear leg/bogie count is preliminary (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.funcDef: Provide wheel braking and directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc brakes, electrically signalled and hydraulically actuated, normal from HYD B, alternate from HYD A, accumulator-supported emergency; anti-skid per wheel pair; in: brake pedals/autobrake, wheel speed; out: brake temperature to AVI (SDD §5.6.2). Independence: dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator sized to six full applications with all three systems lost (SDD §5.6.3, §5.4.3).

functions.funcDef: Provide wheel braking and directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with mechanical disconnect for towing; in: tiller/pedal command; out: steering (SDD §5.6.2, §5.6.4). Independence: mechanical disconnect for tow separates steering from ground handling (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in hold access via the nose visor and form the forward pressure boundary when closed (SDD §5.7.1). Note: the door structural load path is treated as structure (§5.7.3) and is not authored as a function.
functions.subDef: Twelve rotary latches and eight locking pins on two hydraulic supplies with electric backup, dual dissimilar lock sensing, pressure interlock in series with unlock command; in: pressurisation state, crew/ground command; out: lock status to flight deck and take-off configuration monitor (SDD §5.7.2, §5.7.3, §5.7.4). Independence: sensing harness routed opposite the actuation power at two separated penetrations (SDD §5.7.5).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Nine saddles with two tension straps each, electrically winched and mechanically locked, with a continuous tension monitoring loop; in: loading plan/weight-and-balance, WoW, nose door position; out: strap tension and saddle engagement to flight deck, mass/distribution to CG computation (SDD §5.8.2, §5.8.3, §5.8.4). Independence: loss of any one strap carried by neighbours; hold floor hard points have no redundancy; monitoring loop is a single instrumented run (SDD §5.8.3).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two digital controllers drive two outflow valves (either sufficient) with pneumatic backup and independent mechanical relief; in: bleed air, WoW, door position; out: differential pressure/cabin altitude to AVI and crew oxygen logic, pressure state to nose door interlock (SDD §5.9.2, §5.9.3, §5.9.4). Independence: positive/negative relief valves protect structure independently of the control system (SDD §5.9.2). Hold differential is preliminary (SDD §5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two air cycle packs supplied via a cross-bleed manifold condition the flight deck and hold as separate zones; in: bleed air from four engines/APU, ram air, pack selections; out: conditioned air to flight deck and hold (SDD §5.9.2, §5.9.4). Independence: either pack can be supplied from either side through the cross-bleed manifold; single-pack operation permitted (SDD §5.9.2, §5.9.3).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion where accretion would be unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect surfaces, inlets and probes from ice
functions.subDef: Bleed-air protection to wing leading edges and engine cowls, six independently controlled electrically heated stabiliser zones, individually heated probes/ports/windshields and two ice detectors; in: bleed air, electrical power, TAT/airspeed, crew selection; out: ice protection status/zone health to AVI, ice detection advisory (SDD §5.10.2, §5.10.4). Independence: bleed protection available from either side via cross-bleed; electrical zones independently supplied; two detectors of same type (commonality recorded) (SDD §5.10.3).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Present flight, navigation and system information
functions.subDef: Four display units and two HUDs driven by three display processing units on dual networks, fed by three air data inertial reference units, with dual flight management; any DU can present any format; in: data from every system, nav signals, sensing; out: displays to crew, commands to autopilot/autothrottle (SDD §5.11.2, §5.11.4). Independence: three processors in three separate bays, dual networks share no connector/penetration (SDD §5.11.5).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures, driven by two independent processing channels; in: status from every system; out: prioritised alerts and procedures to crew (SDD §5.11.2). Independence: two independent processing channels (SDD §5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Independent integrated standby instrument provides standby attitude, airspeed and altitude on the DC essential bus; in: independent sensing, DC essential power; out: standby display to crew (SDD §5.11.2, §5.11.3). Independence: shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays (SDD §5.11.3).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous fire detection per engine nacelle and APU (AND logic, degrading to single-loop), overheat detection on bleed ducts and main gear bays, hold smoke detection at nine stations; in: DC essential power, WoW, APU state; out: fire/overheat warnings to crew alerting (SDD §5.12.2, §5.12.3, §5.12.4). Independence: two loops routed on opposite sides of each zone, separately clipped (SDD §5.12.5).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed to either nacelle, plus a dedicated APU bottle discharged automatically on the ground unattended; in: hot battery bus power, fire handle commands; out: discharge status, automatic APU shutdown/fuel isolation on APU fire (SDD §5.12.2, §5.12.4). Independence: discharge circuits on the hot battery bus remain available with all generation lost; hold has detection but no suppression (recorded assumption) (SDD §5.12.2, §5.12.5).

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust increase (malfunction of Generate propulsive thrust)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded thrust rise produces an unintended acceleration / flight-path change; if asymmetric across the 28 m outboard moment arm it also imposes a yawing/rolling moment. On approach/landing an uncommanded increase degrades the ability to arrest on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against the ~1,080 m predicted rollout.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded thrust and retard the affected lever(s) / take manual control; increased workload during a dynamic phase.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is clear (unintended acceleration and possible asymmetric moment) but the provided material does not quantify controllability margin or the take-off/landing performance loss for a single uncommanded thrust increase, so a single class cannot be derived. Confirm whether an uncommanded increase on one engine is bounded by available roll/yaw authority and by the landing-distance margin before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust reduction (malfunction of Generate propulsive thrust)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded loss of thrust on one engine reduces total thrust and, at the 28 m outboard arm, imposes an asymmetric yawing moment equivalent to the engine-out directional-control sizing case; at/after V1 the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the thrust reduction, apply rudder to counter yaw and manage the remaining engines; equivalent to handling a single engine failure.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine, which bounds the single-engine case, but it does not state the resulting classification nor address whether an uncommanded reduction differs from a clean shutdown. Effect stated; class not derivable from the provided material without confirming controllability and performance credit.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Thrust asymmetry not commanded by crew (malfunction of Generate propulsive thrust)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded asymmetric thrust across the outboard 28 m moment arm generates a yawing/rolling moment; asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at that arm is the stated sizing case for directional control, so the condition acts directly against the design-limiting rudder-authority case.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply corrective rudder/aileron and identify/retard the affected engine; workload concentrated in take-off and low-speed phases where directional control is most limited.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD identifies outboard asymmetry at 28 m as the directional-control sizing case, which establishes it as design-limiting, but it does not classify the outcome or state whether authority is exceeded when asymmetry compounds with other conditions. Effect is clear; class left blank pending confirmation of remaining control authority and the worst-case phase.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded thrust drift below crew detection threshold (unaware malfunction of Generate propulsive thrust)
fha.effAc: A slow drift below the crew detection threshold accumulates an unnoticed thrust asymmetry or total-thrust error; with the crew taking no corrective action it can develop into an out-of-trim or performance condition before it is recognised.
fha.effCrew: By definition the crew are unaware and continue normal duties with no corrective action until the drift becomes annunciated or manifest.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The unaware case turns on how large the drift can grow before it exceeds rudder trim authority or annunciates, which the provided material does not quantify. Effect direction stated; class cannot be derived until the bounding accumulated asymmetry and the detection threshold are established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust with symmetric degradation
fha.effAc: Symmetric partial thrust loss reduces total thrust available with no asymmetric moment; it degrades climb and take-off performance and reduces margin, but directional control is unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage a reduced-thrust configuration, adjust the flight plan/performance and select a suitable aerodrome if needed; symmetric degradation avoids the directional-control workload.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided material does not state how much total thrust is lost in the 'partial' case nor the performance margin consumed, so the severity (which depends on remaining climb/take-off capability) cannot be derived. Effect stated as symmetric performance reduction; quantified degradation is missing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric thrust degradation within controllable limits (partial loss of thrust, crew aware)
fha.effAc: Yaw/roll asymmetry from unequal thrust; within the rudder authority sized for an outboard engine failure at the 28 m moment arm, so directional control is maintained; some performance/climb margin reduction.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects asymmetry via engine indication and aircraft response, applies rudder/thrust management, and continues to a suitable aerodrome per the engine-out design case.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects are grounded (asymmetry within sized rudder authority, crew-managed, continue to aerodrome), but classification depends on the aircraft-level worst-case flight-phase outcome and residual margin, which is not fixed in the SDD (thrust-loss magnitude, phase criticality). Left empty for engineering judgment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric thrust degradation outside controllable limits (partial loss of thrust, crew aware)
fha.effAc: Thrust asymmetry exceeding available directional-control authority (rudder was sized for a single outboard engine failure at the 28 m moment arm); loss of controlled flight path is credible, most critically at low speed/low altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew cannot arrest the yaw/roll divergence with available control authority in the worst phase.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: By definition outside controllable limits: asymmetry exceeds the rudder authority the SDD sizes to a single outboard engine at 28 m, so controlled flight path cannot be maintained in the critical low-speed phase — an aircraft effect consistent with Catastrophic. PROPOSED for confirmation; engineer to confirm the worst-case phase drives this class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric thrust degradation developing below crew detection threshold (partial loss of thrust, crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Slowly developing asymmetry accumulates below annunciation/detection; unmanaged, it can grow toward the boundary of controllable directional authority before the crew responds.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties and take no corrective action until the asymmetry becomes detectable, reducing available reaction margin.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The unaware case removes crew mitigation, but the aircraft-level outcome depends on how far the undetected drift can grow before it becomes controllable-limit-critical and on detection thresholds — neither is fixed in the SDD. Cannot ground a class without that; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust generation (all engines)
fha.effAc: Total loss of thrust from all four engines; aircraft cannot sustain flight and is committed to a forced landing/ditching; RAT provides emergency hydraulic/electrical only, not thrust.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute engine-out/forced-landing procedures with no means to restore propulsion.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of all propulsive thrust leaves the aircraft unable to sustain flight — an aircraft effect that prevents continued safe flight and landing, consistent with Catastrophic. PROPOSED for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on ground (erroneous / one-sided reverser during landing rollout)
fha.effAc: Reversers fitted to the two inboard engines only; asymmetric reverse thrust during rollout induces a yawing moment and directional-control demand on a semi-prepared surface with an ~1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout; potential runway excursion if unarrested.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter with steering/braking/reverser stowage; effectiveness depends on surface, speed and the margin between required and predicted landing distance.
fha.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects (directional upset on rollout, excursion potential, crew counter-action) are grounded, but the aircraft-level worst-case outcome depends on the directional authority available on the semi-prepared surface at rollout speeds and the reverse-thrust asymmetry magnitude — not quantified in the SDD. Cannot derive a class; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment
fha.effAc: Uncommanded reverse thrust on an inboard engine in flight produces asymmetric drag/thrust and a yawing/rolling moment; if it defeats the in-flight inhibit (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) the aircraft departs controlled flight unless the crew can counter and isolate.
fha.effCrew: High workload to identify the affected engine, counter the asymmetry with rudder/roll and shut down/isolate.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD gives the in-flight inhibit architecture (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement, mechanical sleeve lock) but does not state the aircraft-level effect of an inadvertent deployment that defeats that inhibit; controllability outcome (recoverable vs loss of control) is not derivable from the description, so severity cannot be classified. Needs FCS/PRP controllability analysis of the asymmetric case. On-ground inadvertent deployment effect is likewise not characterised.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust-reverse deceleration capability
fha.effAc: Reduced deceleration on landing rollout; stopping distance increases and eats into the margin between the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout at max landing weight; braking must absorb the shortfall.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum wheel braking; increased attention to remaining runway/strip on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reversers are fitted to inboard engines only and wheel braking is the primary deceleration means with a stated 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m margin; whether a partial reverse-thrust loss alone exhausts that margin (overrun risk) requires the landing-performance/braking degradation analysis the SDD flags as preliminary and not frozen. Severity therefore not derivable from the description.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of thrust-reverse deceleration
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust contribution to deceleration on landing rollout; all deceleration falls on wheel braking, consuming the margin between the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout at max landing weight.
fha.effCrew: Crew rely on maximum wheel braking; increased monitoring of remaining strip length.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Wheel braking is the primary deceleration means (dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve); whether total reverse loss alone causes an overrun on the semi-prepared strip depends on certified landing performance without reverse credit, which the SDD does not provide and flags as preliminary. Severity not derivable from the description.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Roll response different from that commanded (wrong sense, wrong magnitude, or uncommanded roll) degrades trajectory control; with the maximum blade payload and the engine-out directional-control sizing case, an erroneous roll close to the ground or during the engine-out case threatens controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the mis-response, revert control law / disengage autopilot, and fly the degraded law; high workload especially in approach/landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Roll is provided by dual-actuator surfaces on two hydraulic systems with three dissimilar voting FCCs, so the erroneous-command effect that survives the voting architecture is not derivable from the SDD; the controllability outcome of an erroneous roll (recoverable degraded law vs loss of control) requires the FCS malfunction/controllability analysis. Severity left for engineer to confirm against that analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion with no crew command (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls without command, departing intended lateral flight path; crew must counter with opposite roll input to arrest and recover attitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect divergence via attitude display and aircraft motion, apply corrective roll command; increased workload; recovery expected within available control authority in normal law.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded roll near the ground (takeoff/landing) or during manoeuvre significantly reduces safety margins and imposes high crew workload; the effects support Hazardous. Confirm against MAC limits and available roll authority — a large-amplitude uncommanded roll at low altitude could approach Catastrophic and warrants engineering review. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded roll motion below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Slow uncommanded roll develops undetected; aircraft diverges from intended lateral path and bank angle increases progressively without correction until it exceeds crew detection threshold or envelope protection intervenes.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no corrective action (unaware); by the time the divergence is noticed the recovery task is more demanding and margins are reduced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected divergence that continues unarrested erodes safety margins and, if it develops during approach/landing or reaches a large bank before detection, could progress toward loss of control; effects support at least Hazardous. Whether envelope protection (SF-007) reliably arrests it before it becomes Catastrophic requires engineering confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority within manoeuvre (MAC) limits
fha.effAc: Reduced roll authority but sufficient to remain within required manoeuvre limits; aircraft controllable in roll with reduced margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via degraded-law annunciation; larger or more frequent roll inputs needed; increased workload within manageable bounds.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Authority remains within MAC limits, so the aircraft stays controllable with reduced margin and increased crew workload — consistent with Major. Confirm the retained authority envelope against the engine-out plus blade-payload sizing case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority outside manoeuvre (MAC) limits
fha.effAc: Roll authority reduced below that required for the manoeuvre envelope; aircraft cannot achieve required roll response in some conditions, compromising lateral control particularly in the engine-out or crosswind/approach cases.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of degraded law; may be unable to command required roll rate; workload high and safe continuation of some phases in doubt.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects indicate roll authority below required manoeuvre limits, which is at least Hazardous and could be Catastrophic if it removes control in the sizing case; however the SDD does not quantify residual authority outside MAC limits or whether the aircraft remains controllable, so I cannot ground a single classification. Engineering must determine the retained control envelope before a severity is set.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority developing below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Roll authority degrades progressively without annunciation; the shortfall is not apparent until a roll demand (e.g. crosswind, engine-out, manoeuvre) exceeds the remaining authority, at which point insufficient roll response is available.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally and take no action (unaware); the degradation is discovered only when a roll command cannot be met, giving no opportunity to plan or reconfigure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Because the loss is undetected, its consequence depends on how much authority is lost before a demand exposes it — while still within MAC limits the effect is a reduced-margin controllable state (Major). If the undetected degradation can progress past MAC limits before any demand reveals it, the classification rises; confirm the maximum undetected loss and whether monitoring bounds it. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control authority
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be rolled by any means; no lateral/bank control to maintain wings-level or coordinate turns. With the outboard-engine 28 m moment arm as the directional-control sizing case, an asymmetric event with no roll authority is not recoverable; loss of controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew cannot arrest or command bank; unable to maintain a controlled flight path.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of roll control authority in flight prevents continued controlled flight and safe landing; effects support Catastrophic (objective Extremely Improbable, 1x10^-9/fh). Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches in a direction or magnitude inconsistent with the crew command; potential departure from intended flight path, exceedance of structural or envelope limits, or terrain/obstacle proximity depending on phase. Worst effects at low altitude (take-off/approach/landing) where recovery margin is smallest.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive an unexpected pitch response, must diagnose and counter an erroneous surface command; high workload with limited time near the ground.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous pitch response near the ground can produce an unrecoverable trajectory excursion or limit exceedance; worst-phase effect supports Catastrophic (Extremely Improbable, 1x10^-9/fh). Engineer to confirm; magnitude bound not stated in SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch motion below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: A slow uncommanded pitch drift accumulates below the crew detection threshold; with the crew assumed to continue duties and take no action, the trajectory diverges progressively, potentially reaching an attitude/speed excursion or altitude deviation before it becomes evident.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and continue normal duties; no corrective action taken until the deviation becomes detectable, by which point recovery margin may be reduced.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Outcome depends on drift rate, the time-to-detection, and whether envelope protection (SF-007) arrests it before an excursion — none of these bounds are given in the SDD. Cannot derive severity for the unaware case; confirm detection threshold and protection interaction.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority within MAC limits
fha.effAc: Pitch control still available but at reduced authority within manoeuvre-and-control (MAC) limits; adequate control retained for continued flight and landing, with reduced margin and increased crew effort, particularly in gusts or during the flare.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain pitch control but with degraded response and higher workload; a degraded law would be annunciated per §5.3.6.
fha.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Within MAC limits' implies control is retained, but the SDD does not quantify the reduction, the workload increase, or the residual margin in the worst phase (flare/gust), so the effect cannot be pinned to Major vs Minor. Confirm the retained-authority envelope before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority outside MAC limits (reduced pitch authority insufficient to control trajectory at CG/loading conditions outside the mid-aerodynamic-chord envelope)
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority insufficient to maintain intended flight-path at out-of-MAC loading; potential inability to arrest a pitch excursion or flare, depending on residual authority and mechanical stab-trim reversion.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to fly a degraded pitch axis; may require use of mechanical stabiliser trim reversion; large-payload out-of-MAC case reduces available margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Outcome spans loss of trajectory control (potentially Catastrophic) to a controllable degraded state, and depends on residual authority outside MAC and the mechanical stab-trim reversion capability — neither the amount of retained authority nor the reversion adequacy for the out-of-MAC blade-loaded case is quantified in the SDD. Cannot derive severity without that; leaving blank per abstention. NOTE: this condition is not currently in the SF-004 FCIM.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority developing below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Slow degradation of pitch authority progressing without crew action; residual authority may be exhausted before the condition is recognised, degrading trajectory control in a subsequent manoeuvre or flare.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action; degradation undetected until manifested as inadequate pitch response, reducing time to react.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware (no crew action) case; severity turns on how much authority is lost before manifestation and whether the mechanical stab-trim reversion covers the shortfall. The SDD does not quantify the degradation extent or reversion adequacy, so the aircraft-level outcome (Major vs Hazardous vs Catastrophic) cannot be derived. Leaving blank per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control authority (aircraft cannot control pitch by any primary means)
fha.effAc: Loss of control of the pitch axis; trajectory in pitch cannot be commanded through the primary fly-by-wire path. Only a mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and lower rudder remains — a survivable but degraded means, credited only with all three flight control computers lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew forced onto mechanical stabiliser trim reversion (not a selectable mode; results from loss of all electrical command paths); very high workload with markedly degraded pitch control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of a primary trajectory-control axis. Per the SDD only a degraded mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim remains and is credited only with all three FCCs lost; loss of pitch control authority beyond that reversion prevents continued safe flight and landing. Proposed Catastrophic; the adequacy of mechanical reversion is a design claim requiring substantiation, not established evidence. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command (yaw surface responds incorrectly to pilot/autopilot yaw input)
fha.effAc: Yaw response opposite to or disproportionate to the commanded input; potential sideslip/directional excursion, and in the blade-loaded outboard-engine-out sizing case a reduced ability to trim the resulting yaw, degrading directional control.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter an erroneous directional response; increased workload and possible mis-trim, most demanding in the engine-out blade-loaded case that sizes rudder authority.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Outcome depends on the magnitude and persistence of the erroneous yaw and its coincidence with the sizing directional-control case (outboard engine failure at V1 with maximum blade payload). The SDD identifies that sizing case but does not quantify the erroneous-response magnitude, so severity (Major vs Hazardous) cannot be derived from stated effects. Leaving blank per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no crew command (rudder/yaw surface displaces without pilot or autopilot input)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded sideslip/yaw excursion absent any command; potential directional upset requiring immediate correction, with reduced margin in the blade-loaded and outboard-engine-out conditions that size rudder authority.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an unexpected directional excursion; workload elevated, and correction interacts with the split-rudder segment arrangement and its independent hydraulic supplies.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the magnitude, rate and persistence of the uncommanded yaw and whether it can be countered within the split-rudder authority — the SDD describes the split-segment architecture but does not quantify the excursion, so the aircraft-level outcome cannot be derived. Leaving blank per abstention. NOTE: this condition is not currently in the SF-005 FCIM.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of yaw control authority
fha.effAc: No means to command or arrest sideslip/heading; directional control lost. Against the sizing case (outboard engine failure at V1 with maximum blade payload) the aircraft cannot hold heading and departs controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to counter yaw/asymmetry through any inceptor or reversion path.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated support loss of the aircraft: yaw authority is the sizing case for directional control under outboard-engine-out with max payload; complete loss leaves no reversion able to hold heading in the critical asymmetric-thrust condition. Proposed for engineer confirmation against the flight-control directional-control sizing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority within maintainable authority (MAC) limits
fha.effAc: Reduced yaw authority but heading/sideslip control retained within maintainable limits; margin against the outboard-engine-out sizing case eroded.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via degraded-law/status annunciation; retains directional control with increased workload and reduced margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated (control retained within maintainable limits, reduced margin, crew aware, increased workload) support a significant reduction in safety margin/functional capability without loss of control. Proposed for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority outside maintainable authority (MAC) limits
fha.effAc: Yaw authority reduced below the maintainable limit; insufficient to hold heading/sideslip against the sizing asymmetric-thrust case (outboard engine out at V1, max payload).
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to fully counter asymmetry within available authority; heading control not maintainable in the critical condition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated place available authority below what the directional-control sizing case requires, implying inability to maintain controlled flight under outboard-engine-out with max payload. Proposed Catastrophic for engineer confirmation against the flight-control sizing; if outside-MAC still leaves controllable but severely degraded margin, engineer may revise to Hazardous. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority developing below crew detection threshold
fha.effCrew: Crew assumed unaware and taking no action; degradation develops undetected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft effect: the SDD establishes the yaw function and the directional-control sizing driver but does not state how far authority erodes before annunciation, nor whether an undetected partial loss reaches the outside-maintainable regime and when it would first be revealed (e.g. on demand at an engine-out event). Missing: the yaw excursion/authority-erosion magnitude and the exposure/detection point. Severity left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded yaw motion below crew detection threshold
fha.effCrew: Crew assumed unaware and taking no action; slow uncommanded yaw develops undetected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft effect: the SDD does not quantify the yaw rate or the sideslip/heading excursion an undetected slow uncommanded yaw reaches before it becomes detectable or hazardous. Missing: the excursion magnitude/rate and the resulting flight-path or structural consequence. Severity left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment (asymmetry across sections)
fha.effAc: Rolling/yawing moment from unequal lift and drag left vs right; asymmetry brakes at each section are intended to arrest a runaway section, but an asymmetric configuration between sides degrades lateral-directional trim and increases control workload during the low-speed high-lift phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter with roll/yaw control and may need to adjust approach speed/configuration; increased workload at low altitude.
fha.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD establishes the asymmetry threat and the asymmetry-brake mitigation but gives no aircraft roll/yaw response magnitude, controllability margin, or whether residual asymmetry after brake action is controllable at approach speed. Cannot derive Major vs Hazardous vs Catastrophic without the flight-control sizing / controllability data. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift extension or retraction
fha.effAc: Unexpected change in lift and drag not commanded by the crew; uncommanded extension at high speed risks structural/aerodynamic exceedance, uncommanded retraction at low speed reduces lift margin near the ground.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the mode change and re-establish a safe speed/configuration; workload and startle at a critical phase.
fha.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD does not state high-lift placard/limit speeds, the aircraft response to an uncommanded extension at cruise speed, or the lift loss from uncommanded retraction at V-ref. No aircraft-effect magnitude to derive severity from. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected minor high-lift position error below indication threshold
fha.effAc: Small deviation of actual high-lift position from indicated, below the annunciation threshold; performance computation uses the indicated (erroneous) high-lift position, introducing a small error into displayed take-off/landing performance and stall margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue duties normally on erroneous displayed performance.
fha.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD confirms high-lift position feeds the performance computation but gives no magnitude for a below-threshold error or its effect on stall margin/take-off performance. Cannot state whether the aircraft effect is negligible or significant, so cannot derive severity. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced high-lift with symmetric partial extension
fha.effAc: Symmetric shortfall in high-lift raises stall speed and lengthens take-off and landing distance; on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout the landing-distance margin is reduced, but the shortfall is symmetric so no roll/yaw asymmetry results.
fha.effCrew: Crew fly a higher-speed, longer-distance approach and landing per the degraded configuration; increased workload, procedure required.
fha.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD gives the landing-distance requirement and predicted rollout margin but no relationship between high-lift shortfall magnitude and required distance / stall-speed increase, and no threshold at which the semi-prepared distance margin is exhausted. Cannot derive Minor vs Major without that performance data. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of high-lift on one side
fha.effAc: Loss of high-lift on one side produces a strong rolling and yawing asymmetry at low speed combined with reduced lift on that side, degrading lateral-directional control and stall margin during the take-off and landing phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply lateral/directional control and adjust configuration/speed; high workload at low altitude near the ground.
fha.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD describes four flap sections, full-span slats and asymmetry brakes but provides no controllability margin, roll/yaw authority, or whether a full one-side loss is controllable at approach speed on this configuration. Cannot derive Hazardous vs Catastrophic without the flight-control sizing/controllability data. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift capability — no flap or slat extension available by any means; approach and landing flown in a clean/high-speed configuration.
fha.effAc: Approach and landing must be flown without high-lift, raising approach and threshold speeds and landing distance; against a 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement with predicted rollout ~1,080 m the margin is eroded and landing distance on the semi-prepared strip may be exceeded. Take-off performance is likewise degraded.
fha.effCrew: Degraded law / high-lift loss annunciated; crew fly a flapless approach at increased speed, apply the high-speed landing procedure and may require diversion to a longer/paved surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. SDD ties high-lift to meeting the 1,800 m landing requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout; total loss forces a high-speed approach that erodes that margin and challenges landing distance on a semi-prepared strip — a large reduction in safety margins / higher crew workload consistent with Hazardous. Requires performance analysis of flapless landing distance vs the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement to confirm the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous flight-envelope-protection intervention against a valid crew command — protection acts to oppose or override a correct pilot command.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft effect. SDD describes envelope protection only as a normal-control-law feature with degraded laws annunciated; it does not state protection authority or the aircraft consequence of an erroneous intervention opposing crew command (e.g. failure to achieve a commanded manoeuvre, or a departure). Need the flight-envelope-protection function definition and its authority/override behaviour to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Spurious flight-envelope-protection activation with no underlying command or exceedance — protection engages without cause.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft effect. SDD does not define the protection function's authority or the aircraft consequence of a spurious activation (e.g. uncommanded control limiting/manoeuvre restriction). Need the flight-envelope-protection function definition and its intervention authority to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of flight-envelope-protection function while it is displayed to the crew as active — protection is unavailable but the crew believe it is present.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft effect. SDD states degraded laws are annunciated but does not establish the aircraft consequence of protection being absent-yet-indicated-active (e.g. exposure to an envelope excursion the crew do not defend against). Need the protection function definition and the exceedance consequence to classify; crew-unaware case may drive a higher class than the aware cases.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded flight-envelope protection — reduced protective coverage; protection remains partially available at less than full authority/scope.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft effect. SDD does not define which protections exist or their coverage, so the aircraft consequence of reduced coverage cannot be stated or classified. Need the flight-envelope-protection function definition and its protective scope to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight envelope protection — the aircraft can no longer prevent excursion beyond the flight envelope (stall, overspeed, load-factor, attitude limits) by protective intervention; basic control remains but without protective boundaries.
fha.effAc: Aircraft is exposed to envelope excursion (stall, overspeed, excessive load factor) if the crew commands or a disturbance drives it beyond limits; with the maximum blade payload and engine-out directional case, margins are reduced. Basic control law/reversion remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew must manually respect envelope limits without protective backstop; workload increases, particularly in the engine-out asymmetric case that sizes directional control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loss of a protection function does not by itself cause an accident; severity depends on the residual manual controllability and margins with protections lost, which the SDD does not quantify (it states protection status is annunciated and degraded laws exist, but not the outcome of an excursion). Cannot derive Hazardous vs Major without the controllability/exceedance data. Confirm against §25.1309 and the FCS degraded-law substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous fuel transfer driving mass to the wrong tank — the fuel system transfers fuel in a direction that worsens lateral imbalance or moves CG outside limits, contrary to the intended balancing schedule.
fha.effAc: Lateral wing imbalance and/or CG shift develops; imbalance is annunciated at 1,200 kg and structurally limited to 3,000 kg. If the erroneous transfer continues toward or beyond the structural limit it imposes wing-bending loads and out-of-trim, degrading handling; crew can select manual cross-feed and isolate any tank to arrest it.
fha.effCrew: Imbalance discrete alerts the crew (aware case); crew selects manual cross-feed / isolates the offending tank to stop and reverse the transfer, increasing workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects are annunciated at 1,200 kg and structurally bounded at 3,000 kg, with crew manual cross-feed and tank isolation available to arrest and correct — a bounded, detectable, recoverable condition with increased workload. Proposed Major for engineer confirmation; confirm the structural/handling consequence at the 3,000 kg limit does not reach Hazardous. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded fuel transfer with no command — a transfer or cross-feed occurs with no crew or automatic command, redistributing fuel mass without intent.
fha.effAc: Unintended redistribution of fuel mass causing lateral imbalance and/or CG movement; imbalance is annunciated at 1,200 kg and structurally limited to 3,000 kg. Crew can select manual cross-feed and isolate any tank to arrest the transfer.
fha.effCrew: Imbalance discrete alerts the crew; crew isolates the affected tank / manages cross-feed to stop the uncommanded transfer, increasing workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: As with erroneous transfer, the SDD bounds the imbalance (annunciated 1,200 kg, structural limit 3,000 kg) and provides manual isolation/cross-feed to arrest it — bounded, detectable, recoverable with increased workload. Proposed Major for confirmation. NOTE: this condition is not present in the SF-008 FCIM malfunction cell; add the corresponding FCIM entry. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected imbalance accumulating below the annunciation threshold — lateral fuel imbalance develops without crew awareness because it stays below the 1,200 kg annunciation, with the crew taking no corrective action.
fha.effAc: Imbalance accumulates undetected up to the 1,200 kg annunciation threshold, at which point it becomes the aware case. Below that threshold the imbalance is within the structural limit (3,000 kg) and the aircraft remains controllable; the failure that produces the drift may however continue past annunciation.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties and takes no action until the 1,200 kg annunciation, after which the condition becomes the aware case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on whether the undetected drift is bounded by the 1,200 kg annunciation before reaching a handling/structural consequence, or whether the annunciation itself can fail such that imbalance approaches the 3,000 kg structural limit unannounced. fha.fcDesc: Loss of steering with braking / differential thrust available
fha.effAc: Nose wheel steering lost but ground directional control maintained by differential braking and inboard reverse thrust; reduced precision of directional control, most demanding at low speed and on the semi-prepared strip.
