fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware via differential/cabin-altitude indication (differential pressure and cabin altitude are output to the avionics and crew); responds per procedure, donning oxygen and/or adjusting configuration as required.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD confirms independent mechanical relief bounds structural over/under-pressure and that differential is annunciated, but does not state the magnitude, rate, or physiological/structural consequence of an uncommanded excursion, nor the flight-deck cabin-altitude schedule. The aircraft-level effect therefore cannot be derived to a class. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected slow drift in cabin differential below crew detection thresholds
fha.effAc: Differential drifts slowly; independent mechanical relief still bounds structural extremes, but a slow drift by definition remains below annunciation so no automatic protective response is triggered short of relief-valve limits.
fha.effCrew: Unaware case — crew receive no annunciation and continue normal duties, taking no action regarding the drift; awareness only if/when the drift reaches an alerting threshold or the relief valves operate.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Classification of the unaware slow-drift case requires the flight-deck cabin-altitude schedule, the crew alerting thresholds, and the time available before the drift reaches a physiologically significant cabin altitude — none of which are stated in the SDD (hold differential itself is preliminary). Effects cannot be derived, so severity left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution
fha.effAc: No conditioned airflow to flight deck or hold; cabin/flight-deck temperature and air quality degrade over time. Pressurisation control is a separate ECS function and not directly lost by loss of conditioning distribution.
fha.effCrew: Flight-deck thermal environment degrades; crew workload increases; descent/diversion likely required. No immediate loss of control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight — no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a degraded-environment/diversion outcome but the SDD does not state the flight-deck thermal-endurance limit without conditioning nor whether loss of distribution alone jeopardises safe flight; without that endurance/coupling data the aircraft effect cannot be bounded to a class. Confirm whether TL couples to pressurisation loss.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded conditioning on single-source (single-pack) operation
fha.effAc: Reduced conditioning capacity; hold conditioning runs a reduced schedule; flight deck maintained at reduced margin.
fha.effCrew: Manageable with reduced conditioning; single-pack operation is a permitted configuration per the design.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied — no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule, implying a benign/minor outcome, but does not state the resulting flight-deck effect or any operational limitation, so the class cannot be derived without over-reaching to a benign value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of conditioning to one distribution zone
fha.effAc: One conditioning zone (flight deck or hold) loses conditioned air while the other is retained; flight deck and hold are separate conditioning zones.
fha.effCrew: If flight deck is the affected zone, crew thermal environment degrades; if hold, no occupant impact and only conditioning-schedule effect.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied — no occupant effect if hold is the affected zone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on which zone is lost and on the flight-deck thermal-endurance limit, neither bounded in the SDD; cannot derive a class without that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous air temperature or flow to a conditioned zone
fha.effAc: Conditioned zone receives incorrect temperature or flow; flight-deck environment driven hot/cold or over/under-supplied.
fha.effCrew: Crew discomfort and increased workload; corrective selection or reversion to manual mode available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied — no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD supports a degraded-environment outcome with manual mode available, but does not bound how far erroneous conditioning can drive the flight-deck environment or whether it can incapacitate the crew, so the class cannot be derived without that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected contaminant or fume introduction into distributed air
fha.effAc: Contaminant or fume introduced into conditioned air distributed to the flight deck; crew oxygen masks with integral smoke goggles are available on crew action.
fha.effCrew: Potential crew exposure to contaminant/fume; crew don quick-donning full-face masks with smoke goggles; workload and diversion likely. Undetected onset delays crew response.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied — no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on the crew depends on fume toxicity, concentration and time-to-detect, none of which the SDD bounds; the outcome could range from nuisance to crew incapacitation. Cannot derive a class without contaminant-source and exposure data — this is an operational/data gap, not a benign finding.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Ice protection active without accretion, imposing a performance penalty (erroneous/unnecessary activation)
fha.effAc: Wing anti-ice bleed demand reduces pack capacity and imposes the wing anti-ice performance penalty; displayed performance is automatically penalised. No loss of a required function.
fha.effCrew: Crew see the performance penalty applied and can deselect if in manual; increased monitoring only.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effect is a bleed/performance penalty with the penalty automatically reflected in displayed performance (SDD 5.10.6) and deselectable; a modest reduction in capability with no safety-of-flight loss supports Minor. Engineer to confirm the penalty magnitude does not compromise obstacle/climb margins in any phase. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Ice detection indicating falsely with system commanded on (false detection, automatic activation)
fha.effAc: Automatic activation on false detection imposes the anti-ice performance/bleed penalty with penalty automatically reflected in displayed performance; no required function lost.
fha.effCrew: Nuisance ice-detection advisory; crew may revert to manual and deselect; increased workload/monitoring.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Same aircraft effect as the erroneous-activation case (bleed/performance penalty, automatically displayed) plus a nuisance advisory; a slight increase in crew workload with no loss of safe flight supports Minor. Confirm the false advisory does not desensitise the crew to a genuine detection. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of protection on a zone whose failure is not annunciated
fha.effAc: An unannunciated loss of protection on a surface, inlet or probe permits ice accretion where accretion is unacceptable, without the crew being alerted; the aircraft effect (handling degradation, inlet distortion, or erroneous air data from an unheated probe) depends on which zone is affected and the icing exposure at the time.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no annunciation for the affected item and continue normal duties, taking no protective action against the developing accretion.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states a lost electrical zone IS annunciated (§5.10.3), so the affected 'not annunciated' zone and the aircraft consequence of undetected ice on that specific surface/probe are not established. Missing: which zones lack annunciation and the icing handling-qualities / air-data consequence of undetected accretion, per zone. Do not assume a class without this.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected false ice-detector output masking real accretion (detector fails to indicate present accretion)
fha.effAc: A detector failing to indicate genuine accretion, with the system in automatic, leaves protection uncommanded while ice accumulates on unacceptable surfaces/inlets; the aircraft consequence (handling/performance degradation, engine inlet effects) depends on the surface protected and the icing severity encountered.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no ice advisory and, in automatic, the system does not activate; crew take no action unless they independently recognise the icing conditions and select manual on.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: two ice detectors of the same type are installed (common-type item recorded, §5.10.3) but the SDD does not quantify the aircraft handling/performance or inlet consequence of undetected accretion, nor whether the crew can independently detect the icing environment and manually activate. Missing: icing consequence data per protected surface and crew-detection assumption. Do not reach for a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ice protection — loss of a subset of protected zones
fha.effAc: Loss of protection on a subset of surfaces/inlets/probes; the lost zone is annunciated, so remaining zones stay protected and the crew is aware the subset is unprotected. Aircraft effect is unacceptable accretion permitted on the affected subset if the icing envelope is entered.
fha.effCrew: Crew are annunciated the lost zone and can avoid or exit the icing envelope, or select manual on where available; increased workload and possible in-icing operating restriction.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is annunciated (§5.10.3), so a crew-managed degradation, but the aircraft consequence of losing a SPECIFIC subset of zones in icing (e.g. a probe/static heat loss driving air-data error versus a single stabiliser zone) spans a wide severity range and is not established by the SDD. Missing: per-zone criticality and the handling/air-data consequence of that subset unprotected in the icing envelope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one or more electrically heated zones (stabiliser leading-edge / probe / detector zones) with wing and cowl bleed protection retained
fha.effAc: Ice accretion permitted on the affected electrically heated surface(s) while primary aerodynamic surfaces remain protected by bleed; degraded margins on the affected zone in icing conditions. Loss annunciated per SDD (a lost zone is annunciated).
fha.effCrew: Zone-loss annunciation presented; crew assumed to exit or avoid icing conditions per procedure. Aware case.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to payload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level severity from the function definition alone: the SDD does not state which surfaces are lost, the aerodynamic/handling consequence of accretion on the stabiliser or a lost probe/detector zone, or the icing-envelope exposure. Severity depends on that missing effects and exposure data — left EMPTY per abstention rather than reaching for a benign value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of probe, static-port, windshield or ice-detector heating with wing/cowl and stabiliser surface protection retained
fha.effAc: Loss of heating on probes/static ports risks erroneous or lost air-data sensing in icing; loss of ice-detector heating degrades the detection advisory that commands automatic ice protection; windshield heating loss degrades forward visibility in icing. Surface (wing/cowl/stabiliser) protection remains available.
fha.effCrew: Heated elements monitored individually per SDD; affected loss assumed annunciated, crew acts on air-data/detection degradation and may select ice protection manually. Aware case.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to payload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the effect spans several distinct outcomes (air-data corruption vs lost detection advisory vs windshield visibility) whose aircraft-level consequence and icing exposure are not stated in the SDD, and the interaction with air-data (SF-017) redundancy is undetermined. Left EMPTY pending the effects and exposure that would drive the class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ice protection capability (no surface, probe or detector protection available)
fha.effAc: No protection against ice accretion anywhere it is required; in the icing envelope of the certification basis, unchecked accretion on lifting surfaces, inlets and probes degrades aerodynamic performance, air-data integrity and engine-inlet condition simultaneously, with potential loss of control margin if icing conditions are encountered and not exited.
fha.effCrew: Total loss assumed annunciated; crew assumed to exit icing conditions and divert. Result depends on whether icing can be avoided; if entered before detection, controllability and air-data are jeopardised.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to payload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is bounded by icing-envelope exposure, which the SDD references but does not quantify ('the icing envelope of the certification basis'), and by whether crew can reliably avoid/exit icing. Without the exposure and the aerodynamic/air-data consequence of unchecked accretion, the class (potentially Hazardous or worse if icing is encountered) cannot be responsibly fixed — left EMPTY per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous flight or navigation information (attitude, airspeed, altitude, position) presented to the crew as valid
fha.effAc: Erroneous primary flight/navigation data presented as valid can drive the crew or autoflight toward an unsafe state (loss of control, controlled flight toward terrain, envelope excursion) if the crew act on it before the error is detected. An independent standby instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays provides an independent comparison to detect and reject the erroneous primary data.
fha.effCrew: Crew cross-check against the independent standby instrument and against the three air-data inertial reference units; on disagreement the erroneous source is identified and rejected, and the standby data flown. Aware case relies on that cross-check succeeding within available time.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to payload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on whether the erroneous primary data is detectably in disagreement with the independent standby and the triplex reference units before the crew act — an aware, detected error is far less severe than misleading data accepted as valid (potentially Catastrophic if undetected). The SDD establishes the independent standby but not the detection timeline, coverage, or whether a single erroneous source can be common to displays and standby. Left EMPTY pending that architecture/detectability determination; do not default to a benign class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous system information (system status / parameters other than primary flight and navigation data) presented to the crew as valid
fha.effAc: Erroneous system status or parameter data presented as valid can lead the crew to mismanage a system, take an inappropriate configuration action, or fail to respond to a real condition, with an aircraft-level effect that depends on which system's information is corrupted and whether the alerting system flags the disagreement.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on displayed system information; the consolidated prioritised alerting on two independent processing channels may or may not flag the corrupted data depending on the source. Aware only if the error is detectable.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; not applicable to payload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft-level effect is undetermined: 'system information' spans every consuming system, and the consequence of a given erroneous parameter is not bounded by the function definition alone. Which system's data, and whether the alerting cross-check catches it, drives the class. Left EMPTY per abstention rather than assigning a mid-scale or benign value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous flight or navigation parameter presented as valid without a disagreement indication
fha.effAc: Crew fly to an erroneous attitude, airspeed, altitude or navigation parameter believing it valid; with no disagreement flag the crew have no cue to cross-check the standby instrument, risking loss of control or terrain/obstacle conflict in IMC in the low flight levels.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on false information with no alerting; workload and confusion rise once physiological or secondary cues conflict; recovery depends on unprompted cross-check.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Undetected erroneous primary flight/nav data with no disagreement cue can lead to unsafe flight-path deviation in IMC before the crew independently cross-checks the standby; misleading-primary-data effects at aircraft level are typically Hazardous. Confirm against effects and §25.1309 (Hazardous ↔ Extremely Remote, 1e-7/fh). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous system information presented as valid
fha.effAc: Crew act on false system status (e.g. configuration, fuel/CG, gear or door state) believing it valid; with no disagreement cue an incorrect dispatch or configuration decision may go uncorrected, with consequences depending on which system is misrepresented.
fha.effCrew: Crew make decisions on wrong information with no alerting; error may not surface until an independent indication conflicts.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the function definition ('present flight, navigation and system information') does not identify WHICH system's information is misrepresented, and the aircraft effect ranges from benign to severe depending on the parameter. Severity left empty pending the specific system-information set in scope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of a subset of display or information sources with remaining displays and standby information retained
fha.effAc: One or more display units or information sources lost; any display unit can present any format and the independent standby instrument remains, so a valid flight-path picture is retained on reduced displays; increased crew management but continued safe flight and landing.
fha.effCrew: Crew reconfigure displays reversionarily (manual selection); workload rises but required information remains available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Loss of display/information redundancy with valid information retained on remaining displays plus the independent standby reduces margins and raises crew workload without loss of a safe flight-path picture — consistent with Major. Confirm against effects and §25.1309 (Major ↔ Remote, 1e-5/fh). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one air-data/inertial reference source with two reference sources retained
fha.effAc: One of three ADIRUs lost; two independent references retained plus the independent standby instrument, preserving comparison/voting and a valid flight-path picture; degraded redundancy but continued safe flight and landing.
fha.effCrew: Crew note the annunciated source loss; minor increase in monitoring; no immediate action affecting flight path required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Loss of one of three references, with two retained plus independent standby, erodes redundancy and comparison capability without loss of valid data — typically Major. Confirm against effects and §25.1309 (Major ↔ Remote, 1e-5/fh). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of navigation or flight-management information with attitude and airspeed information retained
fha.effAc: Navigation/FMS information lost while attitude, airspeed and altitude remain valid on primary and standby; crew revert to raw-data/basic navigation with increased workload; continued safe flight and landing.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage navigation manually and reduce reliance on FMS; workload rises, particularly in approach; no loss of ability to control the flight path.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Loss of navigation/FMS information with attitude/airspeed retained is a workload increase and slight reduction in capability with valid control information preserved — consistent with Minor. Confirm against effects and §25.1309 (Minor ↔ Probable, 1e-3/fh). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight, navigation and system information presentation
fha.effAc: Aircraft loses the primary presentation of flight, navigation and system information to the crew; per the SDD the independent standby instrument on the DC essential bus, sharing no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries, remains available to present attitude, airspeed and altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses primary displays and consolidated system/navigation information and must fly and navigate on the standby instrument alone with greatly increased workload and no primary system status.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects grounded in AVI purpose (acquire, process and present the information the crew needs) and the independent standby instrument that survives; however whether continued safe flight and landing on standby alone across all phases yields Hazardous versus Catastrophic depends on residual navigation capability, phase-specific reliance and workload not established at aircraft-function level — left empty pending crew-workload/continued-safe-flight substantiation rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Alert mis-prioritisation presenting a lower-priority alert above a higher-priority alert
fha.effAc: The consolidated crew alert list orders alerts incorrectly, so a more urgent condition is presented below a less urgent one; the underlying conditions themselves are unchanged.
fha.effCrew: Crew may address the wrong condition first or delay response to the higher-priority condition, with the consequence set by whatever time-critical condition is displaced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Alerting is an enabler; the aircraft-level outcome depends on WHICH higher-priority alert is displaced and the criticality of the condition it governs, which the AFHA function definition (consolidate and prioritise crew alerting) does not bound. Severity left empty — classification requires identifying the worst-case displaced alert, not a benign default.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Spurious alert presented with no underlying condition
fha.effAc: The alerting system presents a warning or caution for which no real system condition exists; no actual system state is degraded.
fha.effCrew: Crew is drawn to a non-existent condition, potentially initiating an unnecessary procedure or diverting attention from valid indications; workload and distraction increase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect grounded in the consolidated-alerting function, but the aircraft-level consequence of a false alert depends on which procedure it provokes and whether attention is diverted from a real time-critical task; not bounded by the AFHA function definition. Severity left empty rather than defaulted to the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to annunciate a real system condition (missing alert)
fha.effAc: A real system condition exists but is not annunciated; the crew receives no alert and no indication that the alerting function has failed to present it.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties unaware of the underlying condition and takes no mitigating action, so the condition develops unchecked with the consequence set by whatever real condition went unannunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is the unaware case: crew take no action. Aircraft-level severity depends on the worst-case real condition that goes unannunciated (e.g. a fire, envelope-protection loss or imbalance), which the AFHA alerting function definition does not bound. Severity left empty — a missing alert on a Catastrophic-governing condition is not benign, so no default is appropriate.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one alerting processing channel with consolidated crew alerting retained
fha.effAc: No aircraft effect; alerting continues on the remaining independent processing channel. Redundancy is reduced (now single-channel) but the consolidated prioritised alert list remains available to the crew.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain consolidated alerting and associated procedures; loss of the redundant channel is annunciated. No change to crew workload for managing the aircraft.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated: alerting retained on remaining channel, redundancy reduced, condition annunciated — a slight reduction in safety margin with no operational consequence, supporting Minor. Confirm against the alerting DAL/availability requirement. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of consolidated crew alerting
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft trajectory or systems, but the aircraft-wide means of annunciating system failures and presenting associated procedures is lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew lose consolidated, prioritised alerting for every system; failures elsewhere may go un-annunciated or unprioritised, degrading the crew's ability to detect and respond to subsequent conditions. Significant workload increase to monitor systems directly.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated: loss of the aircraft-wide failure-annunciation and procedure-prioritisation means degrades crew detection/response to subsequent failures across all systems, a large reduction in safety margin with significant crew workload increase — consistent with Hazardous. Confirm whether standby/local annunciation limits the effect. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of a subset of standby attitude, airspeed or altitude
fha.effAc: No aircraft effect while primary displays remain; the standby is a reversionary source that shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays. Reversion capability is degraded by loss of one or more standby parameters.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain primary flight information; awareness that reversionary standby coverage is reduced. No immediate change to control of the aircraft.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects stated: primary flight information retained, only the independent reversionary source is partially lost — a slight reduction in safety margin, supporting Minor. Confirm the standby's role in the combined display-loss case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous standby attitude, airspeed or altitude presented as valid
fha.effAc: Potential for erroneous control inputs if the standby is being used as the reference, though the standby is intended as an independent cross-check/reversion against the primary displays.
fha.effCrew: Crew presented with erroneous standby data; a disagreement against the primary displays is available and provides a cross-check, allowing the crew to identify and disregard the faulty source. Increased workload to resolve the discrepancy.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aware/detectable case depends on whether the crew are using primary displays as the working reference and can cross-check the disagreement; the SDD states the standby shares no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries (supporting detectability) but does not define how the standby is used operationally or the crew procedure on standby-vs-primary disagreement. Cannot derive severity without that operational input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous standby parameter presented without disagreement against primary displays
fha.effAc: If the crew are relying on the standby as the reference (e.g. after loss of primary displays) with no disagreement to flag it, erroneous attitude/airspeed/altitude could drive erroneous control inputs with potential loss of control.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on erroneous standby data believing it valid; with no disagreement presented, the error is undetected and no corrective cross-check is triggered.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Worst-case standby error (undetected, no disagreement) is potentially Catastrophic IF the standby is the sole reference at the moment of use (i.e. primary displays lost) — but the provided material does not establish the operational context in which the standby is the working reference, nor the probability of coincident primary-display loss. Effects support a severe outcome but the driving operational context is not grounded, so severity is left empty for engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of standby flight information (independent standby attitude, airspeed and altitude)
fha.effAc: Loss of the independent backup attitude/airspeed/altitude source; primary display and reference chain remains available, so the aircraft continues to be flown on the primary suite with the dissimilar/independent standby fallback removed.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain full primary displays; loss of the independent cross-check reduces the means to detect and reject an erroneous primary parameter, increasing reliance on the primary chain.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries; with the full primary suite available its loss is a reduction in independent redundancy and cross-check capability rather than an immediate unsafe state — significant reduction in safety margin / functional capability. Confirm against the intended dispatch credit for the standby chain. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: False fire or overheat warning presented with no underlying fire or overheat condition
fha.effAc: Spurious warning prompts a fire drill on a healthy zone — potential unnecessary engine or APU shutdown, agent discharge and diversion; on a four-engine aircraft a single unnecessary shutdown is tolerated but reduces installed thrust and available reserves.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute a non-normal / fire procedure against a non-existent condition, with associated workload and diversion decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An unnecessary in-flight engine/APU shutdown and diversion driven by a false warning is a significant reduction in functional capability with increased crew workload, on an aircraft that retains three engines — proposed Major; confirm whether crew procedure permits cross-check before shutdown, which could lower the effect. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to warn on a real fire or overheat condition (crew becomes aware by other means)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD describes the detection architecture (dual-loop, AND logic degrading to single loop) but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an undetected/unannunciated real fire in a nacelle, APU or bleed run; without the fire-progression / structural or control-path effect the aircraft and crew effect cannot be grounded, so severity is left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to warn on a real fire or overheat condition (both detection loops lost silently; crew unaware)
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no fire-response action, as no warning is presented.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware case: an undetected real fire that is never annunciated could progress unchecked, but the SDD does not state the aircraft-level outcome (structural, control-path or propagation effect) of an undetected nacelle/APU/bleed-duct fire; the effect and therefore the classification cannot be grounded on the provided material and are left empty pending the fire-effect determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire/overheat detection coverage in a subset of monitored zones
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect depends on WHICH zone loses coverage (engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed duct, gear bay or hold smoke) and on whether a fire occurs there while undetected; the condition text does not fix the affected zone and the SDD does not state the outcome of losing coverage on a specific zone, so the effect and severity cannot be grounded and are left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of overheat detection with fire detection retained (bleed-duct and main-gear-bay overheat coverage lost, engine/APU/hold fire detection unaffected)
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Taxi
fha.effAc: Undetected bleed-duct or main-gear-bay overheat may progress to duct/structural damage or a wheel-well thermal event without annunciation; fire (as distinct from overheat) is still detected, so a developed fire would still warn.
fha.effCrew: Crew not alerted to an overheat precursor and take no isolation action (reduce bleed / inspect) until a secondary effect or a full fire warning appears.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states overheat detection is fitted to bleed ducts and gear bays but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an UNDETECTED overheat (whether it credibly reaches a hazardous duct rupture, gear-bay fire or structural event before the retained fire detection warns). Effect severity depends on that progression, which is not given. Requires engineering judgement / thermal analysis to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of hold smoke detection with engine/APU fire and overheat detection retained (nine-station hold smoke detection lost, nacelle/APU detection unaffected)
fha.effAc: An in-hold smoke/fire event would go unannunciated; the hold carries no suppression, so detection is the sole means of alerting the crew to a hold fire and enabling the diversion decision. Engine and APU fires are still detected and extinguishable.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no hold-fire warning and continue normally; the diversion decision that the detection-only architecture depends on cannot be taken until a hold fire produces other symptoms.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft-level severity turns on the credible consequence of an UNDETECTED hold fire in a hold with no suppression, which the SDD deliberately records as an assumption to be substantiated rather than resolves. Loss of the sole warning for an unsuppressed compartment could be significant, but the effect (fire progression to structural/control-run damage) is not stated. Requires substantiation of the no-suppression decision to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection (all zones: engine nacelles, APU, bleed ducts, main gear bays, hold)
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Taxi
fha.effAc: No fire or overheat in any monitored zone is annunciated; a fire in a nacelle, the APU compartment, a gear bay, a bleed run or the unsuppressed hold could develop unchecked to structural, control-run or flammable-fluid involvement with no warning and no crew opportunity to actuate extinguishing.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of any fire origin; no fire-handle action, no extinguisher discharge, no diversion triggered by the detection system.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Total loss of the sole means of detecting fire/overheat across all zones — including engine and APU fire zones with flammable fluid and high energy, and an unsuppressed hold — removes every fire warning and the ability to time extinguishing action; an undetected in-flight fire is a classic Catastrophic-potential condition. Maps to Extremely Improbable (1e-9/fh). Confirm against a fire-scenario assessment. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishing-agent discharge into a fire zone with no fire present
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Taxi
fha.effAc: Agent expended into a nacelle or the APU compartment with no fire depletes a finite two-bottle-per-engine-pair charge, reducing the extinguishing reserve available should a real fire subsequently occur in that pair; no direct damage from the discharge itself is stated.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive a discharge indication without a preceding fire warning; may need to reconfigure and account for reduced agent availability for the remainder of the flight.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the aircraft-level effect is loss of extinguishing reserve for a later real fire, but the SDD does not state the residual reserve after an inadvertent discharge (cross-plumbing means the other bottle of the pair may remain) nor the consequence if a real fire then occurs with reduced agent. Severity depends on that residual-capability question. Requires engineering judgement to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Extinguishing agent discharged into the wrong protected zone (wrong nacelle of the engine pair, agent routed by cross-plumbing to the nacelle not on fire)
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Taxi
fha.effAc: Agent delivered to a zone that is not on fire while the actual fire zone receives none; the real fire in the intended nacelle continues to burn while extinguishing reserve is consumed on the wrong side of the pair, so a nacelle fire may go effectively unfought.
fha.effCrew: Crew have actuated the fire handle expecting suppression; the real fire is not extinguished and the crew must recognise the mis-delivery and manage a continuing fire with the pair's reserve partially or wholly spent.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Mis-routing agent so a genuine nacelle fire is not extinguished while reserve is consumed leaves a real fire in a flammable-fluid, high-energy fire zone effectively unfought — a severe reduction in safety margin approaching an uncontained fire. Maps to Extremely Remote (1e-7/fh) if crew retain a means to manage the fire; confirm whether the surviving cross-plumbed bottle can still reach the correct nacelle, which would bound the effect. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing capability (no agent delivery to any engine nacelle or the APU compartment on demand)
fha.effAc: An engine or APU fire cannot be extinguished by any means; fire may propagate uncontained in a nacelle or the APU compartment (zones 610-640, 800), threatening structure, fuel and adjacent systems. Detection remains but the crew has no extinguishing response.
fha.effCrew: Fire warning presented; crew pull the fire handle for fuel/isolation but agent does not discharge. Crew must divert and expedite descent with an uncontrolled fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncontrolled engine/APU fire in a fire zone with flammable fluid present and no means to extinguish can lead to structural/fuel-fed fire and loss of the aircraft; proposed Catastrophic for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced extinguishing agent availability (fewer than the full complement of bottles/shots available to a fire zone)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft effect: the SDD states two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed but does not state whether a single available bottle assures extinguishing of a nacelle fire, nor the number of shots required. Without knowing whether reduced availability still extinguishes, no aircraft effect (fire extinguished / not extinguished) can be stated, so severity cannot be classified from effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one detection loop degrading the discharge trigger to single-loop logic
fha.effAc: Detection AND logic degrades to single-loop; extinguishing capability itself is retained. Warning may be raised on a single loop (loss of the AND cross-check increases susceptibility to a false trigger, but agent delivery on a real fire remains available). Condition is annunciated.
fha.effCrew: Loss of one loop is annunciated per the degraded single-loop logic; crew retain fire-handle discharge and act normally on a warning.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Extinguishing function retained and condition annunciated; effect is a degraded detection margin with dispatch/maintenance consequence, not a loss of protection. Proposed Minor for confirmation. Note: primary effect is on the detection function (SF-020); classified here only on the annunciated degradation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of one detection loop reducing warning coverage
fha.effAc: One detection loop lost without annunciation; warning coverage is reduced and, combined with the AND logic, a real fire may not raise a warning until the second loop responds or may go unwarned on the affected path — delaying or preventing the extinguishing response.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally, unaware coverage is reduced; a real fire may be warned late or not at all, delaying fire-handle discharge.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The extinguishing-function aircraft effect depends on whether the surviving loop still warns a real fire (latent single-loop with AND logic). The SDD states AND-to-single-loop degradation for a KNOWN loss but does not state the warning behaviour for an UNDETECTED loop loss, so whether a fire goes unwarned cannot be derived; severity left blank pending that architecture detail.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Agent fails to discharge on demand with no discharge-status feedback
fha.effAc: On a real fire warning the crew commands discharge via the fire handle but agent does not deliver to the affected nacelle/APU, and no discharge-status feedback reveals the failure; the crew believe the fire is being fought while it continues uncontained in a fire zone (flammable fluid present).
fha.effCrew: Fire warning presented and crew action taken, but crew receive no indication the discharge failed; they may delay diversion/descent believing the fire is suppressed, worsening the outcome.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Failure to extinguish a real engine/APU fire in a fire zone, masked by absent discharge feedback, allows an uncontrolled fire to propagate; proposed Catastrophic for confirmation. NOTE: the listed phrasing ("loss of one detection loop") in the FCIM row reads as a detection effect; this row is classified on the extinguishing malfunction — please reconcile the FCIM text with the intended condition. — engineer to confirm.
